오늘 미국 대형주(SPY)는 홀드 상태를 유지했으나 기술주 중심 나스닥(QQQ)은 매도 전환되었고, 비트코인(BTC)은 홀드, 금(GLD)도 홀드로 중립을 지켰다. 반면 채권 전 구간(TLT, IEF)은 동시 매도 신호를 내며 금리 상승 압력을 반영했고, 달러 인덱스(UUP)는 홀드로 방향성을 유보했다. 원자재 복합(DBC)과 원유(USO)는 나란히 매수로 진입해 인플레이션 헤지 자산에 매수세가 몰렸고, 천연가스(UNG)만 홀로 매도되며 에너지 내 차별화가 나타났다. 농산물(DBA)과 구리(CPER)는 홀드로 횡보 중이다. 전체적으로 주식·채권이 약세로 기울고 원자재·에너지만 강세를 보이는 분산된 추세 구조가 확인된다.

As National Debt Shatters WWII Record, Treasury Market Hits Milestone Last Seen Before 2008 Crash - 24/7 Wall St.
Danielle Liverance · 2026-07-23T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The article analyzes a rare, sustained rise in long-term U.S. Treasury yields (notably the 30-year at 5%+ for a 27th day this year, longest since 2007) despite Fed easing. Main drivers are sticky inflation, higher real yields (30-year TIPS at 2.93%), and heavy issuance from AI-driven data-center corporate debt crowds out buyers for Treasuries. Federal debt held by the public has surpassed 100% of GDP for the first time since WWII, with the CBO projecting 108% of GDP by 2030. Treasury issuance has ballooned from about $4.5T in 2007 to ~ $31T now, contributing to higher long-end yields as borrowers compete for capital. The environment is reminiscent of pre-2008 conditions but with notable differences: a positive 10-year/2-year spread (~0.36%), and a VIX around 17, indicating tempered concern. The article flags potential risks ahead over the next two quarters: auction dynamics, the Fed’s policy pause, and the fiscal trajectory. If demand for long-term debt wanes while issuance rises, the 5% level could become the floor rather than a ceiling.

U.S. 30-year yield set for longest run above 5% since 2007, raising Washington’s interest rate bill - The Globe and Mail
www.theglobeandmail.com · 2026-07-23T00:00:00.000Z

U.S. long-term yields, especially the 30-year Treasury, are at multiyear highs and remain above 5% for a 14th straight day—the longest stretch since 2007. Key points: - 30-year yield: ~5.1637% (up about 1.67 bps). Sustained above 5% signals a rich long-term borrowing cost for the government and suggests investors demand a hefty premium for extended risk. - Broader curve: 10-year at ~4.679% (up ~2.19 bps); 20-year ~5.189% (up ~1.89 bps). Shorter-term rates (e.g., 2-year around 4.315%) remain highly responsive to Fed expectations. - Fed expectations: Markets price roughly a 33.7% chance of a rate hike at the upcoming Fed meeting (up from ~11.8% prior week). - Drivers: Elevated oil prices and geopolitical tensions (U.S.-Iran, Red Sea threats) support risk premiums; despite softer inflation in June, policymakers’ rhetoric remains hawkish, implying higher-for-longer policy. - Demand and market dynamics: Some caution about long-duration demand; domestic policy unpredictability and a shift toward diversified allocations are cited as reasons investors are re-evaluating long-term U.S. assets. - TIPS/tips auction note: 10-year TIPS auction recently saw high tailing (weak bid relative to prior trading levels), suggesting softer demand in some long-duration inflation-protected debt. Bottom line for the outlook: - The 30-year yield staying above 5% indicates persistent long-term borrowing costs and elevated risk premia, even as some data show inflation cooling. If Fed remains hawkish and geopolitical tensions persist, longer-dated yields could stay elevated or rise further, influencing mortgage rates, corporate borrowing, and long-dated asset valuations.

30-year yield raises alarm in longest run above 5% since 2007 – Orange County Register
Bloomberg | wordpress@medianewsgroup.com | Bloomberg · 2026-07-22T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: US long-term Treasury yields are remaining stubbornly high, with the 30-year yield climbing above 5% for the longest stretch since 2007. Key drivers include a rising fiscal deficit/debt burden, heavy AI-related corporate debt issuance, and demand for compensation on the longest maturities amid inflation concerns. The long end has outperformed other maturities in staying above 5%, even as the Fed’s policy rate sits well below this level. Market participants expect continued long-end issuance strategies and potentially larger coupon auctions by 2027. Some observers warn this could reflect a structurally higher long-term yield regime, with “bond vigilante” style pressure possible if fiscal dynamics worsen. Shorter to intermediate maturities (2–10 years) have risen less dramatically, while belly (5–7 year) maturities are favored by money managers to limit risk. The real yield on 30-year bonds has risen toward the highest levels seen since 2008, underscoring concerns about inflation persistence and the sustainability of large deficits.

Executive summary – Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
www.iea.org · 2026-07-21T23:46:10.210Z

Executive summary tailored to your query: commodities market outlook analysis - Global critical minerals focus: Minerals essential for energy, tech, and national security are increasingly prioritized due to supply chain concentration and geopolitical risks. Resilience, diversification, and secure supply are now central government concerns. - Price dynamics (2025–early 2026): - Base metals (aluminium, copper, tin): Prices up ~33% from Jan 2025 to Apr 2026; copper hit record highs. - Battery materials: Recovered after downturn in 2023–2024; lithium prices more than doubled on strong energy-storage demand and constrained supply; cobalt up ~130% due to DRC export restrictions. - Strategic minor minerals: Prices surged in 2024–2026 amid export controls and robust demand (e.g., tungsten up ~6x; gallium and heavy rare earths in Europe ~5x Chinese prices; germanium ~3x). - Regional price gaps: Export controls and geographic concentration created price divergence between China and other regions (Europe especially faces higher prices for certain critical minerals). - Demand–supply outlook (next decade): - Copper and lithium deficits persist through 2035, though deficits are expected to be smaller than previously thought thanks to new projects (copper deficit ~25% in 2035; lithium deficits persist). - Cobalt risk increases due to new DRC export quotas, illustrating how producer policy shifts can rapidly alter tight, concentrated markets. - Investment trends (2025): - Overall critical mineral investment fell 9% after years of growth; battery metals declined sharply (caps down >20%, lithium ~40% lower). Copper investments rose ~8%, signaling confidence in copper’s long-term prospects amid demand. - Strategic diversification opportunity (high-impact takeaway): - Despite extreme concentration, strategic minor minerals can bolster supply security with moderate investment if paired with strong policy support. - Diversifying magnet rare earths would require roughly USD 60 billion over the next decade—substantial but far smaller than potential costs of disruption in high-impact supply chains. - A targeted approach—prioritizing a limited number of high-quality projects—can meaningfully boost resilience without the scale of investment needed for bulk commodities. Bottom line for the commodities market outlook: - Short- to medium-term prices remain supportive for several critical minerals due to supply tightness and geopolitical risk. - Persistent deficits for copper and lithium through 2035, with cobalt risk elevated by policy changes in major producers. - Investment retrenchment in 2025 highlights risk tolerance shifts; copper shows relative resilience. - The path to improved resilience lies in focused diversification of supply chains, particularly for strategic minor minerals, balanced by prudent policy and investment planning.

On the demand/supply side, LNG maintenance and regional Gulf operations are offsetting some summer demand gains, reducing near-term upside risk. Overall macro drivers to watch: storage trajectory relative to seasonal norms, continued LNG maintenance impact, and any shifts in Gulf production/demand from Tropical Storm activity.

Natural Gas Futures Forecast: Henry Hub Sinks to $2.86 Two-Month Low as Record 110.5 Bcf/d Output and a Storage Glut Overwhelm the Oil Spike
www.tradingnews.com · 2026-07-21T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - Near term: Henry Hub natural gas at $2.86/MMBtu, a two-month low, with a clear downside bias as supply runs at record levels (Lower-48 output at 110.5 bcf/d) and storage sits 6.6% above the five-year average. A break below $2.85 could open further downside. - Demand/supply dynamics: Maxed domestic supply and a storage glut amid cooler near-term weather, ongoing LNG constraints (Freeport outage trapping gas at home) and higher renewable generation suppressing gas-fired power demand. - Longer-term bullish catalysts: 2027 LNG export expansion and rising feed gas demand from US LNG facilities, potential AI-driven power demand growth, and a risk of winter spikes that could lift prices. - Outlook tension: The market currently prices in abundant supply, with a near-term path likely sideways-to-lower unless a catalyst (heatwave, LNG restart) emerges. The longer-term path remains for higher prices toward and beyond the $3.70 forecast average due to LNG expansion and storage dynamics. Bottom line: Near-term macro view favors downside risk and a glut-driven environment, while the longer-term view remains structurally bullish on LNG export growth and potential seasonal spikes.
